quote: I wasn't actually looking to have anything done because I'm not a homeowner.
stewart_read: This is an immediate hard-gate disclosure (not_homeowner) — a DQ signal, not resistance to overcome.
coaching_implication: Rep should recognize this as dq_rules.not_homeowner and confirm the gate cleanly rather than continuing to build rapport around the ad.

quote: Oh, I see. Yeah. I know those ads are kinda crazy.
stewart_read: Rep validates the ad's dishonesty rather than pivoting straight to the actual qualifying question about ownership timeline.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been building rapport before the gate check — but the delay cost 15+ seconds without addressing the stated DQ.
coaching_implication: Address the disqualifier directly and early instead of commiserating about the ad copy.

quote: my father-in-law owns the house, and he has not signed the papers over to us yet.
stewart_read: The ownership transfer is indefinite and dependent on an estate/will process, not a near-term closing — this confirms a hard DQ, not a soft timing issue.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have read this as 'soon to be homeowner' worth a follow-up note, but the details (deathbed, will and trust) show no controllable timeline.
coaching_implication: Recognize indefinite estate-dependent ownership as a hard DQ rather than a schedule-a-followup opportunity.

quote: Do you have any idea what pretty much on his deathbed, and it's everything's in will and trust.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a father-in-law nearing death; rep's response is a flat acknowledgment with no empathetic pause.
coaching_implication: This is a vulnerability disclosure (family/health) — schema calls for acknowledging specifically before moving back to logistics; rep skipped straight to process talk.

quote: Well, yeah, you would definitely qualify. What I could do I know sometimes it just with our processes, it's
stewart_read: Rep offers a vague future callback with no locked date/time, an unstructured attempt to keep the lead alive.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep may be trying to leave the door open for a genuinely future-qualified lead rather than push a doomed appointment now.
coaching_implication: If keeping the lead warm, propose a specific concrete follow-up trigger (e.g., 'call us once the deed transfers') rather than an open-ended note.

quote: No. No. No. No. No. No. When the time comes, I will contact whoever I will choose
stewart_read: Customer explicitly declines any follow-up and asserts control over future contact — the call should close here, not push further.
coaching_implication: Accept the decline cleanly and close politely; do not attempt further persuasion after a repeated, emphatic no.
